status: final: zombie, orphan, and dead checks run on the whole v6.6 tree with the shared tristate Kconfig solver (tools/kconfig_solver.py, commit d61cc5d); every error-level dead finding rechecked under 19 other architectures' Kconfig (tools/lint_multiarch_recheck.py) and the 50 that remain classified by reading Kconfig

zombie.method: CONFIG_X referenced in an analyzed Makefile/Kbuild condition (obj-$(CONFIG_X), ifeq/ifneq guards folded into object or directory-reach conditions) or hardcoded as a literal '-DCONFIG_X' compiler flag, cross-checked against a regex scan of every in-scope Kconfig file's 'config'/'menuconfig' declarations.
zombie.ground_truth_check: Ran upstream scripts/checkkconfigsymbols.py (read-only, default mode, no --commit/--diff so it never touches git) on the full tree. Of its 809 flagged symbols, only 9 had any Makefile reference at all (the rest are matches inside .c/.h files it also scans, e.g. GPU register-field enum names like CONFIG_128B_SWAPS, out of scope for a Kbuild-conditions checker). Of those 9: 3 are under other-arch Makefiles (arch/s390, arch/arm64, arch/microblaze) so out of scope for this x86 analysis; 1 (CONFIG_SHELL) is a false positive of checkkconfigsymbols itself (it is Make's own $(CONFIG_SHELL) bootstrap variable, unrelated to Kconfig); 1 (CONFIG_DRM_AMD_DC_DCE11_0) is inside a Make comment ('ifdef 0#CONFIG_...', i.e. an 'ifdef 0' with the rest commented out) so not really 'used'; the remaining 4 are exactly the 4 true positives kfold found below. This is a full match: kfold found every genuine Makefile-scope zombie that upstream's own checker also flags.
zombie.why_the_guard_based_scan_alone_found_zer: checkkconfigsymbols' 4 real hits are all literal '-DCONFIG_X' compiler flags baked into ccflags-y/CFLAGS_x.o (e.g. 'ccflags-y += -DCONFIG_CAAM_QI'), not '$(CONFIG_X)' variable expansions -- so they never become a condition atom kfold's Kbuild analyzer tracks, and a scan of only object/reachability conditions genuinely cannot see them. Fixed by adding a second, complementary scan (kind: hardcoded_define) for literal -D flags, over the same declared-symbol table.

true_positives.reasoning: Makefile line 29: 'ccflags-y += -DCONFIG_CAAM_QI', unconditional (no $(CONFIG_...) expansion, no ifeq guard). CONFIG_CAAM_QI is not declared in any Kconfig file in the tree (confirmed by both kfold's declared_symbols scan and upstream checkkconfigsymbols.py). drivers/crypto/caam/ctrl.c, debugfs.c, debugfs.h and intern.h all guard real code with '#ifdef CONFIG_CAAM_QI' / '#if defined(CONFIG_DEBUG_FS) && defined(CONFIG_CAAM_QI)', expecting a real Kconfig-controlled option. Since the macro is always defined regardless of any .config, that code path is unconditionally compiled in on every build -- a genuine, upstream-worthy 'always-on ifdef' bug.

Makefile lines 179-180: 'CFLAGS_ncr53c8xx.o := -DCONFIG_NCR53C8XX_PREFETCH -DSCSI_NCR_BIG_ENDIAN -DCONFIG_SCSI_NCR53C8XX_NO_WORD_TRANSFERS', hardcoded. Not declared in any Kconfig file. drivers/scsi/ncr53c8xx.c:1779 guards a real code block with '#ifdef CONFIG_NCR53C8XX_PREFETCH'. Same always-on-ifdef bug class as CAAM_QI.
Same CFLAGS_ncr53c8xx.o line as above. drivers/scsi/ncr53c8xx.h:400,408 guards real code with '#ifdef CONFIG_SCSI_NCR53C8XX_NO_WORD_TRANSFERS'. Not declared in any Kconfig file. Always-on-ifdef bug.

Makefile line 4: 'ccflags-y += -DCONFIG_FORCE_HARD_FLOAT=y', hardcoded and unconditional. drivers/staging/rtl8192u/r8192U_core.c:13 guards code with '#ifndef CONFIG_FORCE_HARD_FLOAT'. Not declared in any Kconfig file. Always-on-ifdef bug (here always taking the '#ifndef' false branch).

arch_only_sample_verified.reasoning: Gates 'sa1111_cs-$(CONFIG_ASSABET_NEPONSET) += sa1111_neponset.o'; ASSABET_NEPONSET is a real Kconfig symbol declared only under an ARM (StrongARM/SA1100) board Kconfig. Correctly not-a-zombie (declared, just for arm).

Not referenced in drivers/clk/nuvoton/Makefile itself; found via the directory-reach scan because drivers/clk/Makefile has 'obj-$(CONFIG_ARCH_MA35) += nuvoton/'. ARCH_MA35 is declared for arm64 only. Correct: a real directory guard, correctly arch_only, and it demonstrates the directory-reach ('analysis.reached'/'analysis.builtin') half of the scan is finding real guards an object-only scan would miss.
'obj-$(CONFIG_HAVE_IMX_GPC) += gpc.o'; HAVE_IMX_GPC declared under arch/arm's imx platform Kconfig. Correct arch_only.
'obj-$(CONFIG_SBUSCHAR) += char/' in drivers/sbus/Makefile; SBUSCHAR is declared under arch/sparc. Correct arch_only, again found only via the directory-reach scan.
'obj-$(CONFIG_ARCH_BCM2835) += bcm2835-pm.o'; declared under arm/arm64 Kconfig for the BCM2835 (Raspberry Pi) SoC. Correct arch_only.

zombie.precision_estimate: 4/4 true positives verified by reading the referenced .c/.h source and independently cross-checked against upstream scripts/checkkconfigsymbols.py's own (much noisier, whole-file-corpus) output: 100% overlap, no misses, no false positives in the reported set. 5/5 arch_only sample verified correct. A real bug was found and fixed during this verification: arch_of() mis-labeled arch/Kconfig (~220 architecture-independent symbols: SMP, KPROBES, HOTPLUG_*, ...) as belonging to a bogus pseudo-arch 'Kconfig'; fixed to recognize arch/Kconfig* as common.

orphan.method: .c/.S files on disk with no obj-y/lib-y/rule reference in the cached analysis, supplemented by several text-level heuristics for Makefile idioms kfold's own analyzer does not model (see src/cli/commands/_lint_sources.py docstrings for each).

true_positives.reasoning: drivers/dax/Makefile does not recurse into pmem/ at all; the real dax_pmem driver is drivers/dax/pmem.c (a flat file in drivers/dax/, confirmed present) via 'dax_pmem-y := pmem.o'. The drivers/dax/pmem/ subdirectory (its own Makefile + pmem.c) is unreferenced by anything; its own Makefile even lists 'dax_pmem_core-y := core.o' and 'dax_pmem_compat-y := compat.o' for core.c/compat.c that do not exist in that directory (git ls-files drivers/dax/pmem/ shows only Makefile and pmem.c). Verified this is not a local artifact: 'git status --porcelain -- drivers/dax/' is clean and both files are tracked -- a genuine stale/dead subdirectory in the real upstream v6.6 tree.

false_positives_found.cause: Built via a raw '$(MAKE) -C $(srctree)/$(src)/aicasm OUTDIR=...' recipe command in the parent drivers/scsi/aic7xxx/Makefile (line 87), not the standard '$(build)=DIR' Kbuild submake idiom kfold's rule_closure follows (drivers/scsi/aic7xxx/Makefile also marks 'subdir- += aicasm', explicitly opting this subdirectory out of the normal recursive-descent obj-y model). A real, if narrow, analyzer gap; not fixed (would require modeling arbitrary recipe-line sub-makes, out of scope for a text-level orphan heuristic).
Same cause as aicasm.c (built by the same nested, non-standard sub-make).

lib/raid6/test/Makefile is a completely separate, non-Kbuild, BSD-style userspace test harness ('CC = gcc', its own CFLAGS, invoked manually by a developer, not from any parent obj-y/hostprogs entry) -- the same 'unmodeled nested non-Kbuild sub-build' cause as aicasm.

orphan.precision_estimate: 21/24 (87.5%) of the final residual findings verified as true positives by reading the actual Makefiles (and, for aicasm/raid6-test, confirming a documented non-Kbuild-submake cause for the 3 false positives). This is after fixing the systematic false-positive classes listed in reduction_by_cause, which accounted for 4255 of the original 4279 (99.4%) -- almost all of the raw count. Two of the 21 true positives (usb-skeleton.c, skeletonfb.c) are intentional, low-value example code rather than bugs; the rest (especially drivers/dax/pmem/, the AMD display driver leftovers, and the two s390 zcrypt files) look like genuine, previously-unnoticed dead code.

dead.method: Phi_Kbuild(o) AND Phi_Kconfig(dependency cone of o's symbols) unsatisfiable, with the shared KconfigSMT encoding; undefined-on-x86 symbols pinned to n and then freed to split arch-dead from dead-everywhere

history.cause: kconfiglib reports every tristate as bool when no .config is loaded; the local encoding used .type instead of .orig_type, forbidding m everywhere

dead.bool_composite_container: a composite family's combined object exists only for obj-m; if the family's symbol is bool the container (e.g. net/unix/unix.o) never exists while its members are built. Verified: net/unix/unix.o, fs/iomap/iomap.o absent from the archived defconfig build. Flag now requires the object to have members and only obj-m origins (first heuristic also caught plain obj-$(CONFIG_BOOL) objects: 306 -> 67).
dead.cross_check_predicted: 0 of all dead objects are predicted built under defconfig, allmodconfig, or allyesconfig

precision.x86_error_level_as_dead_code: 45/316 (14%) -- most x86 errors are enabled from another architecture's Kconfig; use tools/lint_multiarch_recheck.py
precision.after_multiarch_recheck: 45/50 (90%) unbuildable in v6.6 on any architecture; 3 toolchain-dependent, 1 UML-only, 1 kfold phantom object

diff_tests.note: See tests/test_cli_lint.py::test_diff_new_zombie_object and ::test_diff_guard_change_fixes_dead_object for the 2 required crafted-patch --diff tests (both pass): one adds 'obj-$(CONFIG_NOPE) += x.o' to a Makefile and confirms x.o is reported 'added' with a new CONFIG_NOPE zombie finding at the exact patched line; the other changes a nested ifeq guard and confirms the previously-dead kbdead.o's condition changes from 'false' to a real satisfiable condition and drops out of the dead findings, while an untouched dead.o stays flagged.
